listX.text: Station-loop range defect: length(station) at L52 uses the largest matrix dimension, not the number of station rows. A one-row, two-column station file therefore iterates twice and indexes past sta_i/sta_j at L53-L55.
Unchecked label offset: station markers use row sta_j(k), but label y coordinates use sta_j(k)-15 at L55. Any station with sta_j<=15 produces a zero/negative MATLAB index; no bounds check exists.
Station indices are used directly against 800-by-660 X/Y without integer/range validation (L11-L13, L53-L55).
The dep binary read assumes exactly m*n singles and does not check fopen/fread success (L16-L19).

listY.text: Station labels are generated as G<14-k> (L54), i.e. G13, G12, ... for k=1,2,...; this presumes exactly 13 stations ordered opposite to the FRF gauge numbering — the actual number of rows in station.txt is not visible here, and if it is not 13 labels go wrong (G0, negative).

Label y-position uses Y(sta_j(k)-15,sta_i(k)) (L55) — an index offset of 15 rows — which errors if sta_j(k)<=15; also mixing an index offset (rows) with the -20 coordinate offset in x is inconsistent.
for k=1:length(station) (L52) uses length() of a matrix, which is max(rows,cols); correct only while the station count exceeds 2 columns.
Stale comments 'make up breaker and foam for visualization' and 'eta without breaker' (L42, L45) are leftovers from the sibling movie script and do not describe this code.
The +220 y-registration matches movie_eta_foam.m but differs from movie_mean_values.m (+180); which is correct for frf_03.jpg is not determinable here.

listX.text: The fixed character slices (6:12, 16:24, 28:36; L13-L17) depend on the exact LOG.txt formatting of the FUNWAVE-TVD directional wavemaker output block; any format change breaks the parser silently (str2double returns NaN).

The header match makes i=1 for every occurrence (L20-L23), so the parser reads only the first data line after each header occurrence and the following line as amplitude — it assumes exactly one component per header repetition; the actual LOG structure is not visible here.

xlim mixes radians and degrees: [-pi/2+theta_mean*pi/180-0.2 ...] is scaled by 180/pi (L47), while the xlabel says theta (rad) and xticks are set at degree values -90:22.5:90 (L58, L62) — units on the axis are inconsistent unless theta_in is in degrees.
E_i normalization by pi (L43) implies a directional bin of pi radians spread; the derivation of this constant is not stated.
freq_resolution uses length(f_i) instead of length(f_i)-1 (L42), a fencepost approximation.
H, theta_pbc are computed/extracted (L35, L37) but never used in the plot.
fp=0.1 and theta_mean=0 (L38-L39) are hardcoded assumptions about the case's peak frequency and mean direction.

listY.text: EOF/order defect across L10-L25: tline is sliced at L13-L17 or passed to strfind at L20 before the non-character EOF test at L25. A header without both following fixed-width data lines can therefore index the numeric EOF sentinel or a short line before EOF is recognized.

Use-before-assignment path across L7-L28 and L30: if no matching header/data block is parsed, output is never created but output(:,4) is immediately read. fopen failure at L5 is also unchecked, and fid is never closed.

Fixed-column parsing at L13-L17 assumes minimum line lengths of 36 and 12 characters and silently converts malformed fields to NaN; there is no length or finite-value validation before downstream arithmetic.

Likely bin-width off-by-one at L42: for N samples spanning f_i(1) through f_i(end) with both endpoints included, uniform spacing is span/(N-1), but the code divides by N, inflating E_i at L43 by N/(N-1). Irregular or singleton f_i is also unhandled.
Angle-unit mismatch across L46-L62: theta_in is plotted against degree tick values -90..90 and x limits explicitly convert radians to degrees at L47, but the x-axis label at L58 says radians.
theta_pbc at L35 and aggregate H at L37 are computed but never used; the figure compares no PBC-direction series despite parsing it.
The figures directory used at L64 and L70 is not created or checked before saveas.

Grid origin values 132.01667/-59.98333 and 0.5-degree spacing are asserted; actual extent depends on depth_30min.txt dimensions not visible here.

MATLAB pcolor at L36 ordinarily renders cells between vertices and omits the final matrix row and column as colored faces; no compensation is present if full-grid coverage is intended.

listX.text: All spectral parameters come from load inputs.mat (L5) — Coherent_Percentage, mcomponent, mfreq, depth, g, fp, gamma_spec, sigma_theta, theta_mean, Hmo are never defined in this file, so the function's behavior is opaque without that mat-file (produced by a sibling script not in this file).
The input arguments idx_theta and freq_in vs the loaded mfreq/mcomponent overlap in role; idx_theta is never used in the function body.

Host selection maps each guest to the nearest host frequency ABOVE it (negative differences set to inf, L35-L37); if a guest exceeds all hosts, min of all-inf gives index 1 — behavior in that edge case is questionable and unguarded.

reps bookkeeping (L42-L43) assigns the host's count to every component sharing that frequency; whether Num_Coherent counts components or frequencies is ambiguous (coherent_idx counts entries with reps>1, L44-L45), so the loop may overshoot the requested percentage.
The while loop can exhaust freqs_pool before reaching Num_Coherent if the count logic stalls; no guard exists (L27-L46).
The comment '% 79.6287' (L70) is an unexplained magic number left in the code.
Hmo_output (L87) is computed as a check but never compared or returned.
The wrapped-normal series truncation N_spec=20/sigma_theta (L72) is not an integer in general; MATLAB's colon operator truncates implicitly.

listY.text: Function-interface violation at L1-L5: load inputs.mat injects hidden dependencies (including Coherent_Percentage, mcomponent, mfreq, depth, g, fp, gamma_spec, sigma_theta, theta_mean, and Hmo) directly into the local workspace and can overwrite same-named explicit inputs. The declared idx_theta input is never used anywhere.

Pool-exhaustion/range defect across L17 and L27-L33: Num_Coherent is not bounded by the achievable pool/count. If the target cannot be reached, mfreq_temp becomes zero and guest_idx becomes zero, making freqs_pool(0) invalid; ceil(rand*mfreq_temp) can also produce zero if rand returns exactly zero.

Invalid-host fallback at L35-L39: when a guest frequency exceeds every host, all freq_diff entries become Inf, yet min selects the first host and the guest is moved to a lower frequency despite the preceding exclusion rule. An empty host_freqs vector is likewise unhandled.

Counting can overshoot or misrepresent the target across L42-L45: reps is propagated to every frequency equal to a host, and coherent_idx counts both hosts and all guests with reps>1. The while condition only requires the count to reach/exceed Num_Coherent, not equal it.

Shape/interface assumptions: reps is sized from loaded mfreq at L21 while indexing uses freq_in/host indices; theta(kf), EnergyBin, and AG assume all loaded/input lengths and orientations agree, without validation.

Singularity checks are absent across L53-L85: nonpositive frequency/fp, nonpositive depth/g, zero sigma_theta, zero Energy_total, zero sum(AG.*EnergyBin), or zero freq_resolution can create Inf/NaN or division by zero. N_spec at L72 is also not forced to an integer before use as a loop bound.
The claimed output-height check at L86-L87 only computes Hmo_output and never compares it with Hmo or raises a diagnostic, so failed energy calibration is not detected.
